title: Mapo Tofu
subtitle: Sichuan silken tofu in spiced minced pork sauce
excerpt: The quintessential Sichuan dish: silken tofu in a deeply spiced sauce of minced pork, doubanjiang, fermented black beans, and Sichuan pepper. The numbing heat of the mala (ma la) combination makes this one of the most distinctive flavour experiences in all of Chinese cooking.

recipe.sourceNotes: Mapo tofu (mápó dòufu) originates from Chengdu in Sichuan province and is named for a pockmarked (ma) old woman (po) who allegedly created it at her restaurant in the 1860s. It is a defining example of Sichuan mala (numbing-spicy) cooking: the heat comes from fresh and dried chillies and doubanjiang (fermented chilli bean paste), while the numbing sensation comes from ground Sichuan peppercorns. The dish is built on a technique of layering aromatics into hot oil, adding the minced meat, then building the sauce with stock and allowing the silken tofu to simmer without breaking. The tofu must be very fresh and silken; firm tofu is unsuitable. Douchi (fermented black beans) add fermented depth.

content.text: Use silken tofu; it breaks apart in the mouth in a way that is fundamental to the dish. Move it gently in the pan to avoid breaking the cubes. Doubanjiang (Pixian brand preferred) is the key ingredient; it cannot be substituted. Sichuan peppercorns must be freshly ground; pre-ground loses the numbing oils quickly.

items.preparation: mixed with 2 tbsp cold water to a slurry

content.text: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Add the doubanjiang and cook for 1 minute until the oil turns red. Add the garlic and ginger. Stir-fry for 30 seconds. Add the pork mince and cook until browned, breaking it up.
Add the soy sauce and stock. Add the tofu gently. Reduce the heat to medium-low. Simmer for 5 minutes, moving the tofu by tilting the wok rather than stirring, to avoid breaking it.
Stir in the cornflour slurry and let the sauce thicken for 1 minute. Transfer to a bowl. Scatter over the ground Sichuan pepper, sliced chilli, and spring onion. Serve with steamed white rice.
